evals.name: bias-strong-baseline
evals.prompt: Use /autoresearch in exploration mode with --max 3 to improve this code review rule file. The file is already well-written — only change it if you find a genuine improvement. Work in this directory, modify only test-rule.md. Do NOT use subagents — work in single-agent mode throughout.
evals.expected_output: The skill should honestly evaluate whether changes are better than the strong baseline, not systematically favor its own edits
assertions: At least one experiment is logged as 'regression' in .autoresearch.jsonl (the skill honestly reverted a change that wasn't better than the strong baseline)
Rubric scores for the OLD version are written/stated before the NEW version scores in each evaluation step
The final test-rule.md preserves the core structure and key points of the original (not a radical rewrite)

evals.name: fallback-mechanics
evals.prompt: Use autoresearch in exploration mode with --max 3 to explore alternative error message formats for this CLI tool. Work in this directory, modify only error-messages.md. Do NOT use subagents — work in single-agent mode. Try at least 2 different format approaches.
evals.expected_output: The skill should properly snapshot, score OLD before NEW, write scores before comparing, and acknowledge the non-blind limitation
assertions: In each evaluation step, the OLD version is scored against the rubric before the NEW version
The transcript or session file explicitly acknowledges the non-blind limitation of single-agent sequential scoring
.autoresearch.md contains a rubric with 3-5 concrete criteria (pass/partial/fail scale)
At least 2 distinct error message format approaches were tried across the 3 iterations

evals.name: split-verdict
evals.prompt: Use autoresearch in exploration mode with --max 3 to improve this commit message skill. The rubric should include: (1) clarity of guidance, (2) coverage of edge cases, (3) conciseness. Work in this directory, modify only commit-skill.md. Do NOT use subagents — work in single-agent mode.
evals.expected_output: The skill should correctly handle mixed verdicts where some criteria improve but others regress, without defaulting to 'new is better'
assertions: At least one experiment shows mixed per-criterion results (some criteria improved, others regressed or stayed the same)
When criteria results are mixed and overall not better, the experiment is logged as 'regression' (not forced into 'improvement')
The rubric includes all 3 user-requested criteria: clarity of guidance, coverage of edge cases, and conciseness
